extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers (especially speculative/fantasy authors) looking for practical worldbuilding advice
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidelines and principles for creating, integrating, and revising fictional worlds that serve narrative, theme, and character. Emphasizes restraint, coherence, and using world detail to support story rather than overshadow it.

rubrics_metrics.name: What We Mean When We Say "Worldbuilding"
rubrics_metrics.description: Revealing story-world details: money, customs, materials, food, cultural practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worldbuilding encompasses concrete everyday details—economics, social customs, material culture—that establish how the world operates and feels.

rubrics_metrics.name: The World Serves The Story, Not Vice Versa
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a world to serve the stories you want to tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize choices that enable character, plot, theme; avoid building elements that exist solely to show off or distract from narrative needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: You're Not Writing A Fucking Encyclopedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive worldbuilding distracts; prioritize narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dumping encyclopedic detail that stalls pace—include only what serves scene, character, or theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Okay, Wait, You Might Be Writing An Encyclopedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Lengthy fantasy epics may use a focused story bible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large-scale epics or serialized worlds, a detailed 'bible' can be appropriate—so long as it's focused and used to support coherent storytelling rather than self-indulgence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variant Approach: Ninja Genesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Build organically as you write, refine in revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider discovering world details in the act of writing and tightening or expanding during revision rather than pre-writing exhaustive lore.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Pig In A Purse
rubrics_metrics.description: Include only details necessary for the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only world elements that matter for plot, character, or theme—extraneous oddities clutter the story and confuse readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function Beyond Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Worldbuilding supports emotional and thematic elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use setting to amplify mood, character psychology, and thematic resonance—not merely as backdrop or logistical scaffolding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action And Dialogue Above Description And Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey world details through interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer revealing world through what characters do and say; let behavior and conflict show how the world works instead of long expository passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Rich Tapestry, Not Plain White Toilet Paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Build complexity beyond simple good-versus-evil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid two-dimensional moral or cultural frameworks; create nuance, contradictions, and layered institutions that feel lived-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Nature Of "Write What You Know"
rubrics_metrics.description: Borrow from understood concepts and translate into fantastical contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use real-world analogues and personal experience as scaffolding—translate, adapt, or invert them to make the imagined world relatable and believable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remix Culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine cultural and mythological influences creatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach cultural borrowing as remix—blend influences thoughtfully and inventively rather than copying wholesale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ew, Stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject monolithic cultural representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lazy or stereotypical depictions; give groups internal diversity and avoid flattening cultures into caricatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Your Heteronormative White Male Gaze
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine presuppositions about gender, race, power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of and interrogate your own biases and default perspectives when designing societies and characters; strive for inclusive, conscientious representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Details Are Just As Important As Big Ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Food, hygiene, craftsmanship reflect cultural values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Micro-details (what people eat, how they clean, how they make tools) reveal cultural priorities and make worlds feel authentic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple Interactions Pregnant With Worldbuilding Complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavior conveys cultural norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use everyday interactions—manners, gestures, expectations—to imply larger social structures and histories without explicit exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Your World Must Be Active And Alive
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals have agency to confirm or deny expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should respond to, challenge, and shape their world; show how institutions and environments affect choices and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: "But It's Cool, Shut Up" Is Not An Excuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Every element must connect to character/plot/theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cool or flashy elements need narrative justification; avoid including things purely for spectacle if they don't matter to the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish clear rules but reveal them through story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the world's rules consistent and intelligible to readers, but avoid info-dumps—let characters' experiences demonstrate constraints and logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wait, I Need To Research My Made-Up World?
rubrics_metrics.description: Research real economics, history, practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even invented systems benefit from grounding in real-world knowledge (economics, agriculture, metallurgy, etc.) to ensure plausibility and consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagine A World On The Edge Of Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Include inherent tensions: war, famine, scarcity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tension and scarcity drive story possibilities—populate your world with plausible pressures and conflicts that motivate characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Everything Affects Everything Else
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize interconnected consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat world elements as systems: changes in technology, economics, or religion should ripple into other domains; avoid one-off conveniences that ignore causal chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtextology
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the world communicate through implication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subtext—what's unsaid, background details, and implication—to convey depth; let readers infer history and norms without overt explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving Mystery Is Vital
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave unexplained elements; resist over-explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain wonder and reader curiosity by withholding some answers; myth and unexplained elements can enrich mood and theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldbuilding Versus Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Robust worldbuilding doesn't guarantee narrative quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember that a detailed world is only valuable insofar as it supports compelling characters and plot; prioritize storytelling craft over exhaustive lore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct Worlds Mapped After Your Own Heartsblood Spatter
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentic passion shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring personal investment and emotional truth to worldbuilding—authentic passion makes setting resonate with readers.
